newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo shares down after in-line profits.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo shares down after in-line profits.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc dropped in early trading on Thursday after the drugs group posted profits no better than analysts expected coupled with a cautious outlook for the next two years.
The stock was down 14-1/2p at 10.20-1/2 by 0803 GMT.
Pre-tax profit rose 18 percent in 1996 to 2.964 billion stg, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range betwwen 2.913 billion and 3.092 billion.
Dealers said there was scope for profit-taking after recent gains in Glaxo shares, which touched a record 10.63 stg in early trade on Wednesday, but the company's longer-term prospects looked solid.

"The company is trading on a discount to other majors in the sector, which is deserved, but once they get over the current hump they will be back to being the premium UK drug company," said one. "The longer term prospects look OK and the question is when do you buy?"
Chief executive Richard Sykes said excluding currency effects the company expected to make "low single digit" sales growth in 1997 and 1998.
Heavy investment would impact trading margins but Sykes said Glaxo expected to maintain current earnings in 1997 and 1998, with "significant growth in 1999."
He said the results showed the company was well prepared to manage in inevitable erosion of U.S. sales of ulcer treatment Zantac following the expected advent of generic competition later this year.
Zantac was expected to decline to as little as 10 percent of total company sales by July 1997, Sykes said.
By 0827 GMT the stock was down 12p at 10.23 stg, in active trade of 1.1 million shares. Yesterday it fell 21p, partly due to a currency-related profits downgrade by Goldman Sachs.
